The wind, a constant companion across the plains, cuts through dry grass and stone alike as the Traveler walks under a baking sun, away from the 
dangerous coastline. Each wary footstep scuffs the dusty soil as they shade their eyes to peer at two fast moving shapes far off in the distance. Though 
small and slender from this far away, the Traveler can still make out the powerful legs of the draffers pounding the earth as they rush headlong into a herd 
of rotund armored rutort insects. Forcing the herd to close in tightly and defend their young larvae, the two cunning mammals circle around, searching 
for any weakness in the impenetrable wall of chitin. 
Knowing it's only a matter of time before the predators look elsewhere for an easier meal, the Traveler slowly lowered themselves to the earth, the Traveler 
slowly lowers to the earth, and hoping the wind doesn’t betray their scent. Though the ground gently rumbles and the dust picks up from the distant 
migrating herd of bloomux, there's a peace to these wide open lands. Picking large seeds near the ground, the Traveler begins to study them, not only to 
document their part in the ecosystem, but if they would make for a handy snack when their supplies begin to run out. 
A vast sky stretches across a wide expanse of earth, only the chain of distant Splitspine mountains breach the unending horizon. As 
clouds paint shadows over the rolling hills and flat plains, a multitude of beasts roam. The Farplains of Sol’Kesh, from the dry arid 
wastes of the west to the flowering fields of the east are home to vast herds of animals, from great chitinous megafauna, countless 
birds, fast moving bipedal predators and patient armored brutes.
On an isolated island, competition for space on the wide open vistas breeds a curious variety of creatures as their range for migration 
can be fairly limited, as well as the distance needed to escape predators. During the millions of years that Sol’Kesh has been separated 
from the continents, certain creatures, once small and unassuming, grew to larger sizes to graze and defend themselves, such as 
the swollen and ponderous bloomux aphid. While others adapted means to break through the tough armors of these generally slow 
moving herbivores — such as the quick footed axilot that's capable of shattering bone with their beaks, or the reptilian grahknash that 
can match any of the herd beasts, pound for pound, tackling them to the soil — the Farplains of Sol'Kesh have become a fierce land of 
brutes.
Rolling hills of dark loamy earth, bisected by the raging Inmere river, spread both north and south in a dizzying array of color and 
sweet scents. For much of the year these fertile plains are nearly entirely covered by blossoming flowers and fungal blooms. This unique 
landscape hosts more nectarivores than anywhere else on Sol’Kesh. Massive bloomux trundle through the flowers sucking deep of 
the nectars, as minute hairs along their six legs collect pollen to propagate the field's diverse flora. All the while, stealthy packs of 
khanith stalk the tall grasses, waiting for one of the slow and thorned beasts to foolishly diverge from their herd. Besides the abundant 
medicinal flowers that a Traveler may harvest, just beneath the soil, ooradew slimemold suffuses large patches of earth, pulled up from 
below by heavily armored Rutort, their long tusks irrigating the earth as they dig. Unaware of the many khanith waiting for them to 
rest their constant vigil. 
A Wide and Distant Expanse
Traveling across the Farplains of Sol’Kesh is inevitable, as it makes 
up most of the island’s landmass. The dangers of such a trek does 
not simply lie in managing to carry enough supplies across the 
parched western lands, or preparing for the torrential rains of the 
east, but truly the greatest danger is being seen. In a land of wide 
ranging hunters, any creature outside a crowded herd is targeted 
as easy prey. For those Travelers brave enough to face these quick 
footed predators, the Farplains of Sol’Kesh are bountiful, from 
some of the best sources of meat, extraordinary extracts from the 
myriad of flowers that spread across the hills, and with the right 
persuasion, a potential mount to ride across these far reaching 
lands.
Elsewhere far from the island, plains stretch across continents 
and creatures spend whole lifetimes migrating from one end to 
simply reach the other. For the creatures that inhabit Sol’Kesh, 
these plains soon run against the coasts or the horizon-
dominating Splitspine mountains that rise from the center like a 
great dividing wall, and so many have learned to keep short and 
constant migrating patterns, following blooming plant growths 
and watering holes.
To survive, many of the slower herbivores adapted to having 
thick, armored hides and roam in close-knit herds to defend their 
young. While the predators that hunt across the Farplains have 
either learned to hunt in packs, or to wait and conserve energy for 
opportunistic ambushes.
More so than any other biome throughout Sol’Kesh, the arthropods 
that evolved eons ago to a lower oxygenated atmosphere have been 
able to grow to monumental sizes on these plains. The rutort and 
bloomux that roam in Valedayn live off the rich fertile flowering 
lands, wary of the nocturnal khanith that lie in wait to pounce 
on any that wander from the safety of the herd. Though not all 
arthropods grew large, and many use their diminutive size to 
their advantage, like the poisonous scorpithine posing in flower 
fields, their pygidium enticing hungry herbivores and pollinators. 
While birds still dominate the sky, two fast moving species found 
another way to speed across the plains. Having both lost their 
ability for flight, the axilot and hectatrex both rush with abandon. 
The small axilot ram their sharp beaks into carcasses like 
voracious barracuda, while the more subtle hectatrex peers over 
the high grasses for nutritious, unguarded eggs, rushing away the 
moment the parents return. While these forms have evolved time 
and time again, there is one genus of bird that have evolved far 
beyond their ancient lineage and now swarm in great numbers, 
descending in a feathered whirlwind to any that find themselves 
beneath the sky darkening cloud of death.
